releases.tagline: A more capable browser, a faster voice, and a simpler start.
releases.summary: Bring the accumulated desktop and web improvements together: persistent per-chat browsing, cloud or local setup, value-based provider routing and cache telemetry, hands-free voice, and experimental verified procedures.
bullets: **Browser built into each chat** — Keep tabs and the selected page scoped to their conversation while sharing the persistent login profile. Browser-first discovery returns readable page content, handles redirects and timeouts, and preserves useful research evidence and source links.

**Lower idle browser overhead** — Bound browser sessions, retire unused agent tabs, preserve user-owned tabs and release idle browser resources. Desktop shutdown cleans up owned workers and bounds background logs.

**Cloud or local first run** — Choose a cloud provider or a local OpenAI-compatible server, discover available models, validate tool calling and then generate a persona. Credentials stay in the local secret configuration; interrupted persona generation preserves the previous active persona.

**Better provider value and cache visibility** — Compare endpoint prices with measured throughput and latency, prefer a fast low-cost endpoint, and retain the same healthy endpoint to reuse its cache. Record actual cached input tokens, cost, time to first token and endpoint identity; missing provider usage remains unknown.

**Stable context and practical tool use** — Keep changing runtime facts outside the stable prompt prefix, reduce repeated instruction and result overhead, and expose browser tools for normal web work. Repair file-edit checks and prevent ordinary documents from being mistaken for outgoing mail.

**Chats stay in order** — Opening a chat no longer makes it look recently active. Actual conversation activity controls recency. Optional low-cost OpenRouter titles adapt to substantive work while preserving manual titles.

**Wake and keep talking** — Configure a desktop wake phrase, listen while minimized or outside Mission Control, and continue speaking after replies. Mission Control stays conversational while delegated workers run and delivers their completion updates once.

**Smoother local voice** — Stream short spoken segments as replies arrive, recover playback and microphone sessions, and reuse warm local audio workers with GPU-aware handoffs. PCM speech detection repairs silent Windows amplitude readings; bounded worker threads reduce idle memory. Cold model startup still depends on the machine.

**Windows lifecycle improvements** — Include the native runner, group helper processes with Liminal when Windows package identity is available, and provide optional local identity registration. Portable ZIP installation continues to use the existing updater.

**Experimental verified procedures** — Explicitly adopt workspace checks, learn bounded JSON-record procedures from verified outcomes, and reuse named inputs through normal tools and approvals. SQLite preserves evidence and versions across processes; dependency drift suspends stale procedures. General productivity gains are not established.

**Browser progress and evidence** — Follow exact observed links, preserve explicit travel dates, read complete result cards and room-rate rows, distinguish crossed-out and current prices, and save bounded research checkpoints. Reordered text queries can match within one passage without combining unrelated columns.

**Clear activity and native startup** — Completed tool groups say Finished; blank narration does not create empty bubbles or split work. Native browser creation reports useful errors, retries once and cleans up failed controllers. Background demos can open their own chat without taking desktop focus.

**Review hardening** — Recover from failed microphone startup and GPU handoffs, bind stored provider credentials to their endpoint, keep tool-budget notices out of later turns, and avoid disabling healthy tools after procedure preflight rejection. Document the native browser local-machine trust boundary and provide a shared-stream opt-out.

releases.tagline: Keep conversations ready after every reply.
releases.summary: Fix a late background trace that could mark a completed reply busy again, leaving subsequent spoken messages queued indefinitely.
bullets: **Terminal busy status** — Desktop and web stop emitting running heartbeats once a turn ends or errors, even while background cleanup is still unwinding. The next real send starts a fresh heartbeat.
**Web chat reactivation** — Reopening a completed chat cannot resurrect its busy indicator during post-turn cleanup.

**Repeated-turn verification** — Regression coverage reproduces late trace ordering and checks subsequent sends. Two consecutive turns against the installed app completed without stale busy events; local Whisper speech and silence checks also passed.

releases.tagline: Warm transcription, reliable hands-free conversations.
releases.summary: Preload the selected local transcription model at startup and repair pause-send, queued speech, recorder lifecycle and recovery across repeated dictation turns.
bullets: **Startup warmup** — Desktop and web load and exercise the selected installed local decoder in the background without opening the microphone, downloading models or calling a cloud provider. A startup-warmed decoder stays resident instead of expiring after two idle minutes.

**Reliable pause-send** — Queued desktop speech is delivered after the agent state clears, in order and to the originating chat. Queued text no longer remains in the composer and gets combined with the next message.

**Continuous dictation recovery** — A failed decode leaves the mic session armed. Uploads and decodes have bounded connections and can be cancelled. Old-session completions cannot reset a newly started session.

**Correct final messages** — The web composer sends the complete final transcript, replacing provisional previews. Final decodes cannot overlap new takes, and speech detection re-arms after completion.

**Windows microphone repair** — Upgrade the recorder backend to include upstream amplitude, streaming and disposal fixes. Pause TTS during actual speech capture as well as transcription. The desktop source build now requires Flutter 3.44 / Dart 3.12; app runtime requirements are unchanged.

**Playback cannot hold the mic forever** — Bound clip loading, player readiness and the playback future itself. Missing native completion signals release dictation instead of leaving it paused after the first reply.

releases.tagline: Local transcription: Whisper speed, optional Qwen accuracy.
releases.summary: Replace the default cloud transcription path with local Whisper Large V3 Turbo and optional Qwen3-ASR 1.7B accuracy mode. Desktop and web share speech gating, language controls and local previews, with no ASR API key required.
bullets: **Fast local default** — Whisper Large V3 Turbo runs on your computer. Optional Qwen3-ASR 1.7B provides an accuracy choice with higher memory and startup costs. Both support managed CPU or NVIDIA installation.

**Speech before decoding** — Neural Silero gating rejects silence and stationary noise. Empty results do not auto-send. Explicit language selection takes precedence over detection; closely related languages can still require a language choice.

**Live local previews** — Desktop and web show bounded provisional microphone transcripts, then decode the full recording once for the final message. Browser-vendor speech recognition is removed from this path.

**Install once** — Use `liminal transcription install whisper --cuda`, or `qwen --cuda`; omit `--cuda` without an NVIDIA GPU. Pinned, verified model downloads persist across updates. Interrupted installers recover dead-owner locks and cancel their owned subprocesses.

**Reliable cancellation and routing** — Ended desktop sessions cannot enqueue a decode after upload. Preview and final language settings agree. Cloud selections remain visible, and local configurations never route to cloud through a per-request override.

**Clear limits** — Models require separate downloads (about 1.6 GB for Whisper, 4.7 GB for Qwen, plus Python dependencies). CPU can be slow. Native Windows Qwen uses Transformers; its timing differs from WSL/vLLM benchmarks. Qwen word timestamps require a separate aligner.

releases.tagline: A warmer JARVIS voice, running on your computer.
releases.summary: Add optional offline JARVIS Warm speech to desktop and web, preserving the original pitch while softening sharp upper frequencies. A one-time installer manages Python, pinned dependencies and verified model downloads.
bullets: **JARVIS Warm, original pitch** — The approved warmer voice profile softens upper frequencies and targets a comfortable -23 LUFS output without pitch shifting.

**Optional local setup** — Install once with `liminal voice install`, or add `--cuda` for NVIDIA acceleration. Managed Python avoids requiring a system Python, Git or FFmpeg. Model weights download once (about 3 GB) and remain separate from app updates.
**Offline playback** — Desktop and web use the same local speech backend, with no speech API key and no cloud speech fallback. Explicit local playback remains available with single-model chat.

**Reliable voice changes** — A serialized warm worker handles cancellation, timeouts, closed input pipes and idle cleanup. Voice/model-aware caching prevents replaying old cloud voice clips after switching.

**Clear limits** — This is an experimental small-data voice adapter. CPU inference can be slow; CUDA is optional. Source provenance, upstream model licensing and the normal Chatterbox watermark are retained.

releases.tagline: Grounded artifact analysis, with a repaired REA backend.
releases.summary: Repair the observed REA 6.4/IDA headless readiness and cleanup failures, add complete validation for the observed recursive archive profile, preserve exact native code evidence, and verify saved findings before handing work back. Unknown formats and undecoded asset structures remain explicit.
bullets: **Native backend recovery** — An explicit, version- and fingerprint-pinned local repair handles valid busy health, advances owned headless analysis, waits for acknowledged worker cleanup, and distinguishes decompiler limits from malformed responses. Original files are backed up. The verified PS2 ELF32 little-endian MIPS profile is admitted while engine and license requirements remain in force.

**Complete archive validation** — Inspect and extract the observed tagged recursive name-table profile with full index coverage, directory boundaries, alignment and extent checks. Return a complete inventory and portable read-only Python reference parser; do not guess formats from extensions or claim decoded meshes from strings.

**Evidence that survives long work** — Preserve partial investigation checkpoints, measured header fields and validated index milestones. Keep exact MCP responses and verbatim pseudocode artifacts with hashes and evidence identifiers; bounded JSON-pointer views retrieve saved details without replaying analysis.

**Accurate native metadata** — Distinguish virtual addresses, RVAs and file offsets from ELF load segments or PE sections. Expose mapped entry bytes and report ambiguous, truncated or zero-filled mappings as unknown.

**Finished handoffs** — Verify explicitly requested JSON/Markdown files on disk, allow one evidence correction pass, and require acknowledged cleanup of native sessions opened by the turn unless the user requested they remain open. Real timeout and round limits preserve an explicit incomplete handoff.

**Faithful tools** — Coerce and validate plain local schema references without changing provider contracts, match HTTP MCP response IDs and finish SSE responses promptly, and resolve directory listings against the active workspace.

releases.tagline: Artifact work with fewer detours and honest completion.
releases.summary: Repair failures found while benchmarking local PS2 and PC game analysis: bounded binary and disc-image tools, raw-byte metadata, useful retries after script repairs, reliable PowerShell modules and foreground cancellation. Explicitly requested artifact providers must be attempted before a run can claim completion.
bullets: **Direct artifact inspection** — List ISO9660 members and extract a selected file with exact offsets, size and SHA-256. Read bounded hex, typed words and strings without inventing dump scripts. Damaged members and unsupported namespaces stay explicit; originals are read-only and extraction never overwrites files.

**Useful recovery** — Harmless Python os/path inspection works, with a documented Python default for short snippets. Re-activating an active family succeeds. Failed programs do not disable corrected commands. Full canonical arguments, ranges and successful mutations distinguish repetition from progress; repeated program failures get one bounded diagnostic window without changing model or settings.

**Faithful MCP discovery** — Explicit tool names rank ahead of descriptive matches, including queries naming multiple operations. Connector guidance remains scoped untrusted reference data; older stdio connections recover it lazily without replaying calls or changing saved credentials.

**Windows command reliability** — Remove incompatible PowerShell Core system-module roots from classic PowerShell child environments while retaining custom locations. Foreground PTY, pipe and snippet cancellation terminates owned work; intentional background tabs remain available.

**Honest turn state** — Stop and timeout cannot report success or start queued work. Partial narration and unfinished tool pairing survive interruption, and late results cannot corrupt a subsequent turn. A requested named artifact connector gets a bounded completion check rather than being silently skipped.
**Binary-safe metadata** — Hash original bytes in bounded streams; hash-off inspection never decodes or buffers a whole game image. Binary and large-file line-count limits are stated explicitly.

releases.tagline: Long tasks keep working, with each reply in its proper place.
releases.summary: Remove a timer-generated recovery plan that could silently stop successful work at round 40. PowerShell foreground jobs return their own output and real exit status. Desktop and web conversations show narration, tool activity and final replies in chronological order, including saved replay.
bullets: **Chronological conversations** — Keep each assistant update before its corresponding tool activity. Later narration and the final reply appear as separate bubbles. Saved logs retain these boundaries without mixing model reasoning into visible replies.

**Progress without phantom budgets** — Elapsed rounds no longer invent a replacement plan or discard compensation history. Real contract budgets count from contract activation, and a hard stop leaves an explicit incomplete-work handoff.

**Reliable Windows commands** — Run PowerShell foreground commands as owned noninteractive PTY jobs, surface each live job in the terminal, and isolate each command from stale prompts and prior scrollback. Multiline scripts execute as complete commands. UI observer errors do not fail or replay running jobs.
**Honest failure status** — Non-zero exits remain failures even when diagnostic output is long. Interactive terminal tools and background jobs remain available for explicitly persistent workflows.

**Retained command output** — Large or filtered foreground output is saved as a retrievable artifact before the completed terminal tab closes. If saving fails, return the captured output directly without repeating the command.
**Regression evidence** — A 45-round harness fixture, late-plan budget checks, visible pause handoff and real Windows PTY commands cover the reported failure and its fixes.

releases.tagline: Legitimate artifact work starts with evidence.
releases.summary: Treat concrete local inspection, decompilation and preservation requests as hands-on work. Use a reasonable legitimate interpretation instead of assuming piracy from a commercial title or file extension.
bullets: **Tool-first artifact work** — Route selected binary/package analysis to execution and ISO-to-launcher requests to coding. Keep the normal tool surface available instead of classifying these tasks as background Q&A.

**Good-faith task handling** — Inspect the selected artifact, respect stated local-use and ownership context, and distinguish decompilation, emulator launchers and native ports. Avoid unsupported legal claims and accusations; explain actual technical blockers with evidence.

**Existing boundaries retained** — Tool approvals and concrete safety limits remain in place. Conceptual questions, quoted examples and explicit negative instructions do not trigger the artifact fast path.

releases.tagline: REA and local MCP tools, ready when you need them.
releases.summary: Connect installed local MCP servers over native stdio. REA's complete catalog is available through on-demand search, with independent conversation sessions, full schemas, structured Evidence and media artifacts.
bullets: **Full REA catalog** — Discover all 170 tools from the installed REA 6.4 server. Search and load the relevant tools instead of sending every schema with ordinary conversations. Native and platform-specific operations retain their provider prerequisites.

**Native local MCP** — Persist executable and argument settings, keep secrets in environment variables, and run helpers outside the installation folder. Conversations and child dispatchers use independent sessions; stopped turns cancel their active MCP requests.

**Faithful tool contracts** — Preserve root schema definitions, nested references, full descriptions, structured results and binary media. Honor mutation annotations and normal approvals; never replay a failed write automatically.

**Verification** — Linux and Windows CI cover paginated discovery, schema preservation, lazy search, independent sessions, denied writes, cancellation and disconnect handling. The real installed REA server passed static JavaScript and headless IDA native fixture analysis, with owned database cleanup and no target execution.

releases.tagline: Windows updates without Google helper directory locks.
releases.summary: The Google Workspace helper runs from user data rather than the app installation folder, allowing Windows to replace the desktop while the helper remains available. Ordinary HTML tables and document examples are no longer misclassified as outbound email.
bullets: **Windows updates** — Start the Google Workspace helper from a dedicated user-data directory. Its child processes no longer hold the app folder open after the desktop exits, blocking the update's directory swap.

**File writing** — Remove content-based email guessing from write_file. Schematics, dashboards, documentation and email-template assets save normally; file-write approvals, overwrite protection and mail-tool validation remain in place.

**Regression coverage** — A live helper fixture reproduces the Windows EPERM before the fix, then permits the app-folder rename while remaining alive. Linux and Windows CI cover this behavior and the HTML file-writing regression.

releases.tagline: Gmail tools that preserve the server contract.
releases.summary: Fix repeated Gmail label errors caused by client-side field rewriting, reduce redundant MCP schemas, and align Gmail draft, ID and read-only handling with the discovered tools.
bullets: **Correct MCP arguments** — Preserve declared fields such as Gmail displayName, native snake_case keys and fractional numeric values. Compatibility aliases are resolved against the current tool, without adding extra model-facing fields.

**Accurate Gmail behavior** — Recognize replyToMessageId, accept valid plain-text MCP drafts, describe HTML-capable drafts correctly and recover from unknown message IDs with a fresh search instead of replaying backend stack traces. Trash, spam, reply and forward actions are classified as writes. Gmail reads stay fresh after mailbox changes.

**Verified live** — Reproduced the old dispatcher failure, created one uniquely named empty label with the repaired dispatcher and removed it. Gmail search and thread reads passed; no messages were changed or sent. The connected Gmail parameter schemas shrank by 68%.

releases.tagline: Reliable Google sign-in, token refresh and Workspace tools.
releases.summary: Existing Google access refreshes independently of an optional Liminal license. Reconnect checks require usable credentials, and the local Docs, Sheets and Slides service starts with hosted OAuth without requiring a client secret on your computer.
bullets: **OAuth recovery** — An expired optional Liminal license no longer blocks provider-token renewal. Expired or unusable saved Google accounts no longer suppress a requested browser sign-in.

**Google Workspace tools** — Recover the public Google client ID from verified token metadata when needed and supply process-local signing material required by workspace-mcp. Google authentication remains enabled and the service binds only to loopback.

**Clear diagnostics** — Distinguish unavailable or failed token refresh from unreadable encrypted credentials. Includes regressions for expired-token reconnect, license-independent refresh and the hosted form handoff.

releases.tagline: Optional, content-free usage sharing with a clear off switch.
releases.summary: Desktop users can choose to share basic adoption and repeat-use milestones with Vireon. Sharing is off by default and is separate from website analytics and model connections.
bullets: **Your choice** — A one-time hub card offers Share basic usage or No thanks. Change the setting later under About & updates; declining does not restrict the app.

**Basic milestones only** — Report app launches, workspace readiness and completed user-started conversation days with app version, platform and a random installation identifier. No prompts, answers, files, paths, account details or provider keys are sent.
**Useful activity counts** — Ignore transcript replay, background turns, errors and cancellations. Deduplicate each milestone per UTC day; network failures never block startup or conversations.

**Delete and stop** — Turn sharing off immediately or delete that installation’s shared history without an account. Failed deletion stays off and can be retried. Daily records and inactive installation records have a 90-day retention policy.

releases.tagline: Clean shutdown even after Windows closes desktop output pipes.
releases.summary: Desktop-owned sidecars tolerate closed stdout and stderr pipes so parent-exit cleanup can finish. Prevents recursive EPIPE logging from keeping the old runtime alive and blocking the next update.
bullets: **Closed-pipe recovery** — Handle EPIPE on desktop-owned output streams before startup or shutdown logging. Other output errors retain their existing error path, and standalone servers are unaffected.

**Verified process regression** — A real child process with ignored stdin and both output pipes closed now completes its cleanup after parent termination. The unchanged test fails without the fix and passes with it.

releases.tagline: Clean desktop shutdowns keep future updates unblocked.
releases.summary: Desktop-owned sidecars detect when their launching app exits and shut down, releasing the install folder for updates. Standalone and explicitly attached servers retain their existing lifecycle.
bullets: **No orphaned desktop sidecars** — The app identifies its owned sidecar's parent process. If the desktop closes or crashes, the sidecar shuts down even when stdin does not report closure.
**Reliable update preparation** — Release the old runtime's file handles before a future launch update replaces the app folder. Shutdown handles overlapping signals once.
**Real process coverage** — A detached child with ignored stdin is tested against actual parent termination, including in Windows CI. Standalone servers and unrelated process IDs opt out.

releases.tagline: Safer tool recovery and a verified Windows update handoff.
releases.summary: Windows updates launch the Node helper directly and require a startup acknowledgement before closing the app. Includes the completed harness audit repairs for interrupted tools, concurrent writes, guest isolation and public-web requests.
bullets: **Windows update handoff** — Avoid detached PowerShell startup failures. The app waits for the updater to initialize and stays open if startup fails. The helper waits for the old process to exit before replacing files.
**Faster Windows extraction** — Use the Windows archive utility for large app bundles, retaining a PowerShell fallback when it is unavailable.

**Workspace preservation** — Keep extra files and folders created at the bundled workspace root when they are absent from the new release, alongside credentials, preferences and saved workflow artifacts.
**Safe tool recovery** — Preserve eager tool execution across stream recovery and isolate streamed-write manifests and staging files between concurrent sessions.
**Access and lifecycle hardening** — Complete the reviewed fixes for guest chat boundaries, public-web destinations, file operations, locks, provider scheduling and terminal/browser cleanup.

releases.tagline: Faster first answers and accurate file-write status.
releases.summary: DeepSeek hybrid models respect external reasoning mode, latency routing takes effect without stale provider affinity, and desktop file previews finish with clear saved, failed, or unconfirmed states.
bullets: **Faster first answers** — Stop hidden native thinking on supported DeepSeek hybrid models when external reasoning is selected. Native reasoning budgets and mandatory-reasoning models retain their existing behavior.

**Responsive provider routing** — Default new routing to latency, remove the implicit price-sort override, and refresh sticky provider affinity when routing policy or model changes. Existing explicit preferences remain respected.

**Accurate write status** — Successful tool results immediately show saved, failed writes show failure, and interrupted turns stop active indicators without claiming success. Late stream or approval events cannot reopen completed writes.

**Visible verification** — Keep completed file previews available, preserve another active preview during parallel writes, and record harness preparation and first-answer timings separately in session logs.

releases.tagline: Verified automatic updates before your workspace opens.
releases.summary: Liminal checks for complete releases at launch, downloads and verifies the app bundle, then installs and restarts automatically. Offline checks and skipped updates open the current version, with rollback and configuration preservation for installation failures.
bullets: **Automatic launch updates** — Enabled by default for portable installs. Update checks load saved preferences and installed versions before the harness starts, correctly recognize bundled runtimes, and do not interrupt active work after reconnects.
**Clear launch progress** — Download progress and an Open current version option let you continue without installing. Automatic updates can be disabled in About & updates.
**Verified downloads** — Stream archives to disk, require valid SHA256 checksums, reject incomplete responses and partial releases, and reuse verified cached archives.

**Reliable installation** — Run the detached helper outside the install folder, preserve local configuration, prepare the replacement before swapping, and restore the old app if replacement or relaunch fails. Correct the Windows helper PID conflict and macOS bundle destination.

**Recovery without restart loops** — Record a durable automatic attempt before restart; an unsuccessful version requires a manual retry. Check failures and download errors leave the current app usable.

releases.tagline: Three guided workflows with saved deliverables and recoverable progress.
releases.summary: Turn client enquiries into sourced proposals, receipt images into validated expense reviews, and bug reports into tested patches. Includes desktop and web entry points, downloadable deliverables, resumable runs, and reliable Windows terminal regression checks.
bullets: **Enquiry to proposal** — Research primary sources and save a printable proposal, editable Markdown, source list, and unsent reply draft with `/proposal`.

**Receipt to expense review** — Local English OCR, date/currency/arithmetic checks, source hashes, and an optional approved Xero DRAFT with an attached receipt. Xero writes are adapter-tested with fixtures; no live-account certification is claimed.
**Bug report to verified patch** — `/fix` requires a reproduced failure, passing tests after edits, and a fresh Git diff before saving the patch, test output, and handoff.
**Recoverable work** — List and resume saved runs with `/workflows` and `/resume-work`. Retry interrupted receipt uploads against the existing bill ID; resumed patches require fresh verification.
**Desktop and web delivery** — New welcome cards, file buttons, safe web downloads, and receipt submission recovery. Completed workflow checks finish with a concise handoff.

**Windows verification** — Terminal replay checks wait for actual shell output and clean up on failure. A version-pinned node-pty compatibility fix prevents console teardown races and releases the output worker after natural shell exit. Native PowerShell commands preserve their real exit codes. Required npm tests cannot silently pass when scripts are absent; Windows CI covers terminal and workflow checks.

releases.tagline: Searchable OpenRouter models, single-model operation, and a faster response path.
releases.summary: Choose individual OpenRouter models in desktop and web, keep agent work on one selected model, and avoid the extra classifier request before replies. Includes refreshed product screenshots and a rewritten README.
bullets: **OpenRouter catalog** — Search the live catalog by name or model ID, inspect tool and vision capabilities, and select individual models without applying model bundles.

**Single-model mode** — Keep chat, background completions, and vision on the selected model; disable separate embeddings, hosted speech, and automatic model fallbacks while preserving specialist preferences.
**Faster first replies** — Use local intent routing by default, skip unused classifier repo scans, and warm installed-tool inventory at startup. The optional remote classifier remains available.
**Latency visibility** — Separate harness preparation, provider output, and first answer text in telemetry; add a reproducible live benchmark and document its limits.
**Updated presentation** — New desktop and web marketing images, a clearer README, corrected setup guidance, and explicit beta release information.

releases.tagline: A redesigned workspace and simpler settings across desktop and web.
releases.summary: A consistent slate-and-iris interface, a rebuilt desktop hub, and streamlined settings with everyday controls first and searchable advanced options.
bullets: **Workspace redesign** — Shared typography, neutral surfaces, clearer navigation, conversation layouts, and composers across desktop and web.
**Desktop hub** — Recent conversations, a searchable paginated library, mission editor, connected tools, and inbox navigation.
**Simpler settings** — Clear categories, everyday controls, searchable advanced options, and collapsed credentials and technical details.
**Connected tools and onboarding** — Categorized integrations and consistent setup, account, and error screens.
**Reliable web builds** — Browser-safe core entry points prevent server-only dependencies from entering the web client bundle.

releases.tagline: Multi-account mail, inbox watcher, file attachments, integrations hub polish, managed inference fixes.
releases.summary: Scans all connected Gmail/Outlook mailboxes with account-aware replies, automated inbox watcher with Gmail labels, email privacy redaction, composer drag-and-drop for any file type, redesigned integrations panel on web and desktop, and managed inference Settings that stay on managed mode.
bullets: **Multi-account mail** — `mail_search_inboxes` scans every connected mailbox; `account_hint` on Gmail/Outlook compose and send; session `mail_account_context` persists the chosen mailbox across turns (rule **R-EMAIL-ACCOUNT**)
**Connected mail only** — `mail_oauth_filter` ignores unconnected integrations and Entra `#EXT#` guest admin mailboxes; `list_connectors` shows **Connected mailboxes**
**Email privacy** — `email_redaction` masks SSN, cards, phones, and addresses in summaries; `mail_search_inboxes` defaults `redact_sensitive: true` (rule **R-EMAIL-PRIVACY**)
**Inbox watcher** — Background Gmail/Outlook polling with label support; automated receipt workflow hooks; capability gates for mail tools
**File attachments** — Drag, drop, or paste any file into web and desktop composer; `chat_attachments` persists to `.agent_artifacts/uploads/` with limits (12 total: 4 images, 8 files)
**Integrations hub** — Web `IntegrationCard` + per-account list; desktop provider rows, connection status, revoke account; `integrations_snapshot` and `revoke_integration_account` tools
**Managed inference fix** — Settings **managed** mode no longer flips back to BYOK on Pro; sidecar skips BYOK auto-patch when user chose managed; regional Bedrock profile ids in desktop model picker
**Email compose** — Expanded recipient guard, compose context/resume, Gmail compose guard tests; capability gates and long-horizon eval updates

releases.tagline: Desktop auto-update — harness hot-swap and app restart from GitHub Releases.
releases.summary: Portable Liminal Desktop installs can check GitHub Releases on launch, apply harness updates in place (liminald-runtime zip), and schedule full app updates with a one-time restart. CLI gains liminal update --check for portable installs.
bullets: **Desktop auto-update** — Settings → About & updates; hub banner when a newer `v*-desktop` release exists
**Harness hot-swap** — downloads `liminald-runtime-v{version}.zip`, stops sidecar, swaps `liminald/`, reconnects
**App update** — downloads full platform archive, verifies SHA256, relaunches via bundled updater scripts
**Release manifest** — `liminal-desktop-manifest-v{version}.json` on each desktop GitHub Release
**CLI** — `liminal update --check`, `--json`, `--harness-only` for portable installs; git path unchanged

releases.tagline: First public preview release — stability milestone with CI, eval framework, latency optimization.
releases.summary: First tagged public preview. Stabilization milestone: CI workflow on main, eval sandbox framework, inference latency mode, tool circuit for performance, desktop managed inference catalog, and sidecar multi-chat registry.
bullets: **CI workflow** — `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs build, typecheck, and test on every push to main
**Eval sandbox framework** — `packages/eval/fixtures/` sandbox scenarios; `npm run eval:sandbox` for reproducible agent tests
**Inference latency mode** — `AGENT_LATENCY_MODE` patches for performance-optimized inference paths
**Tool circuit** — `tool_circuit.ts` for parallel tool execution optimization
**Kimchi constants** — Extracted `AGENT_KIMCHI_*` constants for Cast AI provider tuning
**Desktop managed inference catalog** — Flutter UI for managed inference model selection
**Sidecar multi-chat** — `chat_registry.ts` for multi-session support
**Inference path validation** — `scripts/validate-inference-path.ts` for diagnosing routing issues
**Release checklist** — `docs/RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md` documents the v0.1.0 release process

releases.tagline: Live compose dock, email HTML preview, Azure ARM, Kimchi provider, OSC 133 shell.
releases.summary: Ships immediate desktop compose preview for file edits and email drafts, rendered HTML in the email dock, expanded Azure Resource Manager REST tools with API-version inference, Kimchi/Cast AI provider throttling and retries, and OSC 133 shell-integration markers for deterministic agent-terminal command completion.
bullets: **Compose dock** — `compose_preview` + streaming `tool_delta` open the right pane immediately on `write_file`/`edit_file`/Gmail/Outlook compose; content streams live and the panel persists through `turn_end`
**Email HTML preview** — Extracts `<body>` fragments and sanitizes for `HtmlWidget`; fixes raw-HTML monospace preview during streaming
**Azure ARM** — Subscription, resource-group, and location tools; per-resource `api-version` inference; clearer OAuth/ARM errors; guide in `docs/guides/azure.md`
**Kimchi provider** — Cast AI rate-limit parsing, transient 400/429 retries, min request interval, throttle-aware circuit breaker; `AGENT_KIMCHI_*` in Settings
**OSC 133 shell** — Prompt markers at PTY launch (`shell_integration_launch.ts`); `agent_shell_session` + `Osc133Tracker` for deterministic command-done events without prompt regexes
**Provider backends** — Kimchi backend routing in `provider_backends.ts`; web/desktop Settings presets updated
**Desktop WebView** — `desktop_webview_lifecycle.dart` pauses off-screen WebView2 instances to cut GPU/memory churn

releases.tagline: Desktop design system, Sheets auto-fit, integration arg reliability, research reply fix.
releases.summary: Ships a Flutter design system and polished Vireon hub + chat UI, harness-side Google/Linear/Sheets tool-arg normalization, automatic Sheets column/spacer sizing after writes, and a structural user-reply finalize pass so research turns end with a chat answer.
bullets: **Desktop design system** — Shared tokens, primitives (Button, Card, Badge), patterns (Sheet, EmptyState, SearchField), persona shells; wired through hub, home, chat panes, composer, and settings
**Vireon hub** — Status strip, quick actions, mission control, searchable chat list, integration chips, two-column layout, pull-to-refresh
**Chat UI** — Distinct user/assistant/tool/reasoning lanes (`chat_message_frame`, `reasoning_block`, `tool_category`); polished composer, drawer, message and tool activity tiles

**Tool arg pipeline** — `prepareToolArgsForValidation` normalizes Google MCP, Google REST, and Linear args before schema validation; fixes Sheets `requests`/`data` JSON-string coercion and MCP HTTP 400 from hallucinated fields

bullets: **Memory curator** — `curate_memory` (dry-run by default) sends a metadata-annotated slice of the note store to the model, which returns prune / merge / re-confidence ops; a deterministic safety-rail veto then protects `user:`/`identity:`/`pref:` keys, high-access, and too-young notes. Deletion is **reversible**: `forget` and the curator soft-delete the full note to `notes.archive.json` (`AGENT_MEMORY_ARCHIVE`) before removing; `restore_memory` recovers it. Tunables: `AGENT_CURATOR_TIMEOUT_MS`, `AGENT_CURATOR_MAX_TOKENS`, `AGENT_CURATOR_PROTECT_GLOBAL` (off — `global` is the default scope, not a durability signal)

**Output effort** — `AGENT_EFFORT` (`low` | `medium` | `high` | `xhigh`) — a deliverable-thoroughness dial injected as a system-prompt directive (rule **R-EFFORT**), exposed as a Settings dropdown. A separate axis from reasoning: it scales completion budget and output completeness/coverage, not internal `think()`/`reason()` depth

**Voice I/O** — Text-to-speech (`speak`, Kokoro / OpenAI voices, per-turn budget + near-duplicate suppression) and live microphone **dictation** in the web UI; voice-mode tool gating. See [Voice I/O](../guides/voice.md)
**Retrieval** — Second-stage recall reranker over first-stage BM25 + embedding hits; fast-model JSON response cache to cut repeat sidecar calls

**Prompt cache** — Rolling `cache_control` breakpoint over conversation history (`AGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_ROLLING`) plus volatile-tail context ordering (`AGENT_CTX_VOLATILE_TAIL`), so the cache extends across accumulated tool-result history, not just the static prefix
**File tools** — `find_files` (path/name glob) and `delete_file` (approval-gated); a catalog reachability test guards against tools unreachable under lazy loading
**Chat UX** — Markdown renderer for assistant output, session screenshot export, persona shell refactor (Hud / Minimal / Studio / Terminal / Composer)
**Web** — Greeting fires on reload without blocking, SSE reconnect robustness; OpenRouter `session_id` on chat completions for request grouping
